subject: PR & supplier steps for Redwood — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: PR & supplier steps for Redwood — next steps

Hi Sophie — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a couple of asks to keep momentum on the procurement side: 

- Recap: You confirmed the use-case (internal clinical insights pilot), expected first-month spend is likely to land above your $5k PO threshold depending on usage, and security/evidence requests were limited to a vendor questionnaire and W-9 for payments.

As we discussed, could you confirm the following so we can prepare procurement-ready artifacts and speed up PR creation: 
1) Do you prefer payment via company card for initial proof-of-concept, or will procurement require a PO from day one? If PO, is the $5k threshold correct?
2) Which marketplace or procurement system do you primarily use for vendor onboarding — Coupa or Ariba (or your internal portal)? If Coupa/Ariba, is there an existing supplier ID we should reference, or will procurement create a new supplier record?
3) Any preferred internal ticketing process or reference (cost center, GL code, internal contact) we should include in the PR to avoid routing delays?

Attaching our standard vendor form and a condensed supplier profile (company/legal name, address, tax id, bank remit instructions) to speed your vendor onboarding team: vendor-form.pdf; redwood-supplier-profile.csv. If you prefer, we can also provide a DocuSign version for signatures.

Next steps I suggest: you confirm PO vs card preference and marketplace, we prepare the supplier docs, and Aditya will open an internal JIRA to track the onboarding steps so nothing slips. Happy to hop on a 15-min call with procurement if that helps.

Thanks — looking forward to your guidance.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

-- Attachment: redwood-supplier-profile.csv (text/csv)

From: Sophie Nguyen <sophie.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PR & supplier steps for Redwood — next steps

Marissa — thanks for the follow-up and the docs. Quick answers from procurement: 

- We route vendor onboarding via Coupa.
- PO is required for purchases over $5,000 (threshold confirmed). For POCs under $5k we sometimes use a corporate card but need prior procurement approval.
- Procurement needs: vendor legal name, W-9, completed vendor onboarding form (attached on our side), and a preferred remit address. Once we have those, procurement will create a supplier record in Coupa and issue a supplier ID which you can reference in the PR.

Two asks from our side: 
1) Are you listed on any cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace, GCP Marketplace)? If so, that can streamline procurement and payments.
2) Please include a suggested GL/cost center line and the contact for Redwood Finance — our team needs a named point of contact to route payment questions.

I attached our procurement checklist for vendor onboarding (procurement-checklist.docx). I cc'd procurement@acmehealth.com to start the supplier record once we have your W-9 and vendor form.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Nguyen
Procurement Manager | Acme Health
sophie.nguyen@acmehealth.com
-- Attachment: procurement-checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PR & supplier steps for Redwood — next steps

Thanks Sophie — really helpful. Quick answers and a step-by-step to avoid back-and-forth on the PR: 

- Marketplace: Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace (listing ID: aws/redwood-inference) — we can provide the marketplace SKU if Acme prefers to transact that way; that typically simplifies purchase orders and billing.
- Redwood supplier info you can reference for Coupa/Ariba:
  - Legal name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
  - Remit / payment email: finance@redwood.com
  - Tax ID: 12-3456789
  - Default remit address: 500 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94105
  - Redwood vendor reference (internal): REDW-100213

Coupa PR guidance (recommended fields to include when creating the PR to link the supplier):
1) Supplier: Redwood Inference, Inc. (search by legal name OR REDW-100213)
2) Payment terms: Net 30 (unless otherwise agreed on PO)
3) Commodity/line item description: Redwood Inference — Hosted LLM inference (hourly tokens) / Pilot license
4) Cost center / GL suggestion: 55-2300-AI (please confirm with your finance team)
5) Attachments to the PR: vendor-form.pdf, redwood-supplier-profile.csv, W-9 (I can provide if procurement prefers), and the signed SOW when executed

If you use Ariba instead, the equivalent is to request supplier onboarding and provide the same documents — most fields map 1:1.

Internal tracking / next steps on our side: Aditya will open JIRA INF-4321 to track the supplier onboarding and procurement approvals; Dev will prepare a short billing contact note for finance@redwood.com. I'll also drop a HubSpot note with the recommended purchase path (PO vs marketplace).

If it helps, I can join a 15-min screen-share while a procurement analyst creates the Coupa supplier/PR — we can be on-hand to provide the vendor ID and answer fields in real time. 

Thanks again — please let us know whether you want to go marketplace or PO route and I will circulate the W-9 immediately.

Best,
